verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā bahudevarattiṁ abbhokāse caṅkamitvā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ pāde pakkhāletvā vihāraṁ pavisitvā
verses.english: He spent much of the night walking mindfully in the open. At the crack of dawn he washed his feet and entered his dwelling.

verses.pali: dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṁ kappesi pāde pādaṁ accādhāya sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṁ manasi karitvā.
verses.english: He laid down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware, and focused on the time of getting up.

verses.pali: Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
You sleep like a loser—<j>what’s up with that?
You sleep, thinking that the hut is empty.
You sleep when the sun has come up—<j>what’s up with that?”
the weaver, the clinger—<j>to track them anywhere.
With the ending of all attachments <j>the awakened Buddha sleeps.
What’s that got to do with you, Māra?”
